education.description: Intensive full-stack web development bootcamp that teaches the fundamentals of programming across the front-end and back-end. Gained knowledge about React, Redux, Node, Express. Worked in a team of four members to build a meal delivery website.

Studied many engineering topics, including digital communication, digital signal processing, real-time applications, robotics, and nanotechnology. Also studied computer science topics, such as computer architecture design, microprocessor applications, model-driven software, and formal hardware verification.

experience.description: Senior software engineer building and maintaining React/TypeScript applications at scale , with additional responsibility stepping into a Product Owner capacity when the team needed it. Owned frontend architecture, built private NPM libraries, and optimized Core Web Vitals, while also driving roadmap decisions and cross-team alignment during critical delivery phases.
highlights: Built and maintained production React/TypeScript features using Styled Components, React Router, Redux Toolkit, and React Query as the primary engineering role.

Stepped into a Product Owner capacity when needed, facilitating sprint planning, translating business requirements into technical specifications, and aligning stakeholders across frontend, backend, and design.
Set API contracts and acceptance criteria at the start of feature cycles, keeping cross-team integration issues from surfacing late in delivery.
Architected and maintained private NPM libraries for UI components and utilities, improving code reuse and reducing duplication across teams.
Ran code reviews and mentoring sessions with junior developers, raising engineering standards and cutting review turnaround time by ~25%.
Optimized Core Web Vitals and enforced accessibility and performance best practices across multiple product lines.
Kept quarterly documentation of team decisions, shipped features, and architectural direction — giving leadership visibility without needing to ask.

experience.description: Worked collaboratively in a team of 4 to develop web applications using React, Material-UI for the frontend, and Express, Node, MongoDB, Cloudinary Image uploader, and JWT authentication for the backend.
highlights: Developed frontend with React and Material-UI, focusing on modular components and responsive design.
Built and integrated REST APIs using Node.js, Express, and MongoDB, including authentication and file uploads.
Implemented JWT authentication and secure user flows.
Participated in agile sprints, code reviews, and collaborative problem-solving.

experience.description: Assisted in developing iOS and Android mobile apps using Expo, TypeScript, Jest, and React Native. Gained hands-on backend experience with Node.js and Express by building and consuming REST APIs and applying core patterns like routing, controllers, and middleware to support the web app rebuild.
highlights: Developed iOS and Android apps using Expo, TypeScript, Jest, and React Native.
Built and consumed REST APIs with Node.js and Express, applying routing, controllers, and middleware patterns.
Supported a major web app rebuild, improving maintainability and performance.
Gained hands-on experience with backend and cloud technologies.

experience.description: Provided technical support for clients across Windows and Mac environments — diagnosing software and hardware issues, configuring network equipment, resolving email issues, and managing the full support lifecycle from intake to resolution.
highlights: Diagnosed and resolved software and hardware issues for clients across Windows and Mac environments, covering OS errors, corrupted installations, driver conflicts, and application failures.

Walked clients through router setup, port forwarding, and home network troubleshooting over the phone — translating technical steps into language non-technical users could follow without repeat calls.
Resolved email configuration issues across multiple providers — account setup, send/receive failures, access recovery, and sync problems on desktop and mobile.
Started in sales for the first six months, handling inbound calls to qualify needs and sell technical support packages in a high-volume phone environment.
Managed the full support lifecycle independently: gathering symptoms, replicating issues remotely, applying fixes, and confirming resolution before closing.

projects.title: ZTable: Interactive Chemistry Platform
projects.excerpt: A frontend-heavy React and TypeScript chemistry app with a searchable 118-element periodic table, a 3D atom model, exact-math equation balancing, and Web Worker offloading to keep complex tools responsive in the browser.
projects.shortDescription: A modern chemistry platform built with React 19, TypeScript, and Vite. It combines dense reference UI with computation-heavy tools including a molar mass calculator, chemical equation balancer, solubility lookup, worksheet generation, and a Three.js-powered 3D atom model. I separated UI, domain logic, and background compute so the app stays maintainable and fast as feature complexity grows.
highlights: Interactive 118-element periodic table with detailed chemistry reference views
Exact BigInt fraction math for equation balancing plus shared formula parsing and caching
Web Worker offloading, lazy loading, and granular Zustand selectors to keep heavy UI responsive

projects.title: Productify: Full-Stack Product Showcase Platform
projects.excerpt: A deployable full-stack TypeScript app where I built Clerk-based authentication, ownership-safe product and comment CRUD, paginated REST APIs, and cache-aware React Query updates that keep the UI snappy without unnecessary refetching.
projects.shortDescription: A full-stack product showcase application built with React, Vite, Express, Drizzle ORM, and PostgreSQL on Neon. It supports sign up and sign in with Clerk, protected routes, synced user records, product and comment CRUD, ownership-based authorization, pagination, and centralized auth token handling. I also worked through deployment-specific issues such as Linux case-sensitive imports, CORS setup, and DATABASE_URL formatting to get the stack running cleanly on Vercel and Render.
highlights: Clerk authentication with protected routes, user sync, and centralized token handling
Ownership-based authorization for product and comment CRUD with paginated REST endpoints
Cache-aware React Query mutations plus deployment fixes for CORS, env config, and Linux import paths

projects.title: zsk-react-i18n: Typed React Localization Wrapper
projects.excerpt: A reusable npm package that wraps i18next/react-i18next with a type-safe API for React apps. I built both factory and direct-provider modes, runtime language guards, localStorage persistence, multi-language scaling, and compile-time translation-key safety backed by tests.
projects.shortDescription: A reusable npm package that wraps i18next/react-i18next with a type-safe API for React apps. I built both factory and direct-provider modes, runtime language guards, localStorage persistence, multi-language scaling, and compile-time translation-key safety backed by tests.
highlights: Factory and direct-provider modes for flexibility
Compile-time translation key safety
Comprehensive unit testing with Jest and React Testing Library

projects.title: zsk-react-error: React Error Boundary & Reporter
projects.excerpt: A TypeScript-first React error boundary and reporter package with advanced error state control, reset logic, and analytics integration. Designed for scalable, production-grade error handling in React apps.
projects.shortDescription: A robust React error boundary and reporter package supporting both global and local error state, composable hooks, imperative resets, and flexible fallback UI. Integrates easily with Zustand and analytics tools for complete error visibility.
highlights: Global and local error state management with composable hooks
Keyed error isolation and imperative reset support
Customizable fallback UI and error reporting integration
Optimized for performance and scalable error handling
Easy integration with Zustand and analytics tools

projects.title: Smart AI: Full-Stack SaaS AI Platform
projects.excerpt: A comprehensive SaaS platform democratizing access to AI capabilities. Provides features for article generation, image creation/editing, resume analysis, and community interaction—with freemium tier distinction enforced at the API boundary.
projects.shortDescription: Full-stack AI-powered SaaS application integrating multiple AI services (Gemini, ClipDrop) and media processing (Cloudinary) with plan-based access control. Features user dashboards, creation history, community feed, and usage tracking.
highlights: Full-stack architecture with Express backend and React frontend
Integrated AI services: Google Gemini (text), ClipDrop (images), Cloudinary (storage)
Plan-based access control enforced server-side with Clerk authentication
User creation history, community feed, and like/publish system
Usage tracking and rate limiting for free tier users
MikroORM for type-safe database operations with PostgreSQL
Comprehensive API routes for AI generation and user management

projects.title: Auto Pause & Media Control: Chrome Extension
projects.excerpt: A zero-dependency Chrome extension that automatically pauses media when you switch tabs and gives you precise scroll-wheel control over volume, playback speed, and scrubbing—no library required, just clean browser APIs.
projects.shortDescription: A lightweight, privacy-first Chrome extension built on pure vanilla JavaScript and the Chrome Extensions API. It intelligently pauses audio/video on tab blur and resumes on return, with scroll-wheel shortcuts for volume, speed, and scrubbing. Includes a Glassmorphism popup UI with individual feature toggles and a master kill-switch.
highlights: Smart Auto-Pause: pauses media on tab switch and resumes precisely on return
Precision Media Scrubbing via Shift+Alt+Scroll using smooth trackpad scaling
Master Volume Control with Alt+Scroll hover gesture
Dynamic Playback Speed (0.25x–4.0x) via Ctrl+Alt+Scroll
Glassmorphism popup UI with per-feature toggles and a master power switch
Zero data collected—pure local JavaScript with no external dependencies

projects.title: zsk-portfolio: This Portfolio (over-engineered by design)
projects.excerpt: The site you're looking at right now. Built as a deliberate exercise in senior-level architecture using React 19, Vanilla Extract, Zustand, and a zero-runtime CSS design system. Every technology choice has a reason behind it — some practical, some intentionally ambitious.
projects.shortDescription: A fully interactive developer portfolio built to showcase architectural decision-making as much as UI craft. Uses a headless JSON data layer, type-safe CSS-in-JS compiled at build time, compound component patterns, PWA offline support, a synthetic Web Audio click engine, and hydration-safe state persistence. Purposefully over-engineered.
highlights: Zero-runtime CSS via Vanilla Extract — styles are TypeScript, compiled to static .css at build time
15+ hot-swappable color themes built on a typed createThemeContract design system
React 19 Compiler integration — automatic memoization, no manual useMemo/useCallback
Headless JSON data layer in /public — fully decoupled from the UI, reusable across any future rebuild
Synthetic click sounds via Web Audio API (no .mp3 files, no network requests)
PWA-ready via vite-plugin-pwa with offline service worker caching
Keyboard accessibility: T (theme), M (mute), Cmd+D (download CV)
Custom NPM packages: zsk-react-error and zsk-react-i18n used in production

projects.title: zsk-use-sound: React Hook for File + Generated Sound
projects.excerpt: A TypeScript-first React hook inspired by use-sound that supports both Howler-powered file playback and browser-generated click sounds through one API. Designed for UI feedback without forcing bundled audio assets.
projects.shortDescription: zsk-use-sound unifies two sound strategies in one ergonomic hook: file mode for mp3/wav assets via Howler, and generated mode that synthesizes built-in click profiles in the browser when no file is provided. It exposes a familiar tuple API with play controls, mode visibility, and sound-enabled toggling for app-wide mute workflows.
highlights: Dual-mode audio engine: file playback (Howler) and generated Web Audio click presets
TypeScript-first API with exported option/play/control types for consumer safety
Built-in generated profiles (click, soft-click, tick) with volume and playback controls
Supports global mute flow via soundEnabled and per-play override via forceSoundEnabled
use-sound-inspired tuple return shape with stop, pause, duration, and runtime mode metadata

projects.title: zsk-jd: AI-Powered Resume Tailoring Skill
projects.excerpt: A portable LLM skill that performs ATS gap analysis, interview probability scoring, and full LaTeX resume tailoring against any job description — with a mandatory warning gate before output and bilingual cover letter generation.
projects.shortDescription: A structured prompt skill for Claude and other LLMs that automates resume tailoring end-to-end: JD parsing, skill gap scoring, ATS keyword injection, and compilable LaTeX output with optional cover letters. Built with strict ATS writing rules, fabrication guardrails, and support for patch-mode diffs.
highlights: Performs weighted skill gap analysis (hard skills 60%, seniority 25%, domain fit 15%) with interview probability estimate
Mandatory warning gate blocks output if match score < 50 or majority of required skills are missing — prevents false confidence
Rewrites professional summary, reorders skills, and injects JD keywords into bullet points without fabricating any experience
Generates standalone compilable LaTeX cover letters in 4 length modes (short, default, long, cover-only) with formal/casual tone flags
Patch mode outputs only changed LaTeX blocks — clean diffs for version control workflows
Strict ATS writing rules: 15+ banned words/phrases, no em dashes, no repetitive bullet structures, no robotic summary openers
Portable across Claude, Cursor, Copilot, ChatGPT, Gemini CLI, and any markdown-capable LLM

projects.title: Coin Gate: Live Crypto Market Dashboard
projects.excerpt: A production-style crypto dashboard built with Next.js 16, React 19, and TypeScript. It combines server-rendered CoinGecko market data with live websocket updates for pricing, trades, OHLC charts, search, and coin conversion in one responsive interface.
projects.shortDescription: Coin Gate is a crypto market dashboard built with Next.js App Router, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Base UI primitives, and lightweight-charts. It includes a home dashboard with featured market views, a paginated coins page, and dynamic coin detail screens with live pricing, recent trades, OHLC charting, and conversion tools. I used server components, client components, route handlers, and websocket subscriptions together so the app can load stable market snapshots first, then layer in live updates without losing responsiveness.
highlights: Home dashboard with featured coin overview, trending assets, and top categories
Paginated coins listing plus dynamic coin pages with live pricing, trades, OHLC charts, and conversion
Shared CoinGecko data layer handling REST, websocket streams, demo/pro API differences, and OHLC fallback logic

projects.title: Z Gym: Premium Fitness Brand SPA
projects.excerpt: A production-style fitness SPA built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI, and Motion. I treated it like a real frontend system, with scroll-driven sections, reusable UI primitives, typed content, and theme support instead of one-off page styling.
projects.shortDescription: Z Gym is a premium fitness brand experience built as a section-based single-page app. It uses React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI primitives, and Motion for scroll-driven storytelling, responsive layout, and polished dark and light themes. For me, this project is a good example of building more than a modern-looking website. It is also structured to be scalable, reusable, and maintainable, with isolated section components, reusable hooks, shared animation variants, direct imports, and a centralized typed content layer that keeps the codebase held to a high standard.
highlights: Scroll-driven single-page experience with responsive section architecture and premium visual pacing
Reusable UI primitives, shared animation variants, and isolated section components instead of page-specific one-offs
Centralized typed content plus theme support and accessible interactions built for maintainability, not only presentation

blog.title: I Ditched Axios for Ky And My Dependabot Finally Stopped Screaming
blog.excerpt: A personal breakdown of Fetch, Axios, and why Ky quietly became my go-to HTTP client in React.
blog.shortDescription: A practical comparison of Fetch, Axios, and Ky through the lens of bundle weight, retries, timeouts, TypeScript ergonomics, and the security cost of unnecessary dependencies.
highlights: Compares Fetch, Axios, and Ky through real React and TanStack Query usage
Breaks down Axios security incidents and supply-chain risk as a decision factor
Explains why Ky became the default request layer for modern React projects

blog.title: Context vs Redux Toolkit vs Zustand: Picking the Right State Tool for the Job
blog.excerpt: You don't need the most powerful state manager. You need the right one.
blog.shortDescription: A production-minded comparison of React Context, Redux Toolkit, and Zustand, focused on re-render behavior, boilerplate, team scaling, and the tradeoffs that matter months after launch.
highlights: Maps the strengths and weaknesses of Context, Redux Toolkit, and Zustand
Explains the Context re-render trap and why selector-based stores feel better at scale
Shows when scoped Zustand plus Context is the right hybrid pattern

blog.title: React Query vs SWR vs the `use` Hook: Why You're Fetching Data Wrong
blog.excerpt: You already know how to fetch data. What you're missing is everything that happens after.
blog.shortDescription: A production-focused comparison of raw fetch, SWR, React 19's `use` hook, and TanStack Query, centered on caching, mutations, race conditions, and why client-side data fetching is really a state synchronization problem.
highlights: Explains where raw fetch and Axios break down once caching, deduplication, and stale data enter the picture
Shows why the React 19 `use` hook is powerful in server components but limited as a client-side data fetching strategy
Compares SWR and TanStack Query through mutations, optimistic updates, DevTools, infinite queries, and real production tradeoffs
